passages.text: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and notes thereto included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. This report contains forward-looking statements which include but are not limited to predictions, future guidance, projections, beliefs, and expectations about the company’s trends, seasonality, cyclicality and growth in, and drivers of, the markets we sell into, our strategic direction, earnings from our foreign subsidiaries, remediation activities, new solution and service introductions, the ability of our solutions to meet market needs, changes to our manufacturing processes, the use of contract manufacturers, the impact of government regulations on our ability to conduct operations, our liquidity position, our ability to generate cash from operations, growth in our businesses, our investments, the potential impact of adopting new accounting pronouncements, our financial results, our purchase commitments, our contributions to our pension plans, the selection of discount rates and recognition of any gains or losses for our benefit plans, our cost-control activities, savings and headcount reduction recognized from our restructuring programs and other cost saving initiatives, and other regulatory approvals, the integration of our completed acquisitions and other transactions, and our transition to lower-cost regions. The forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties that could cause Keysight’s results to differ materially from management’s current expectations. Such risks and uncertainties include, but are not limited to, the impact of global economic conditions such as inflation or potential recession, the impacts of increased trade tensions such as an imposition of or increase in tariffs and tightening of export control regulations, slowing demand for products or services, volatility in financial markets, reduced access to credit, changes in interest rates, the existence of political or economic instability, uncertainty related to the impact of national elections results in the U.S. and U.K., impacts of geopolitical tension and conflict in regions outside of the U.S., the impact of new and ongoing litigation, impacts related to net zero emissions commitments, and the impact of volatile weather caused by environmental conditions such as climate change. Our actual results could differ materially from the results contemplated by these forward-looking statements due to various factors, including but not limited to those risks and uncertainties discussed in Part I Item 1A and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Risks, Uncertainties and Other Factors That May Affect Future Results Risks Related to Our Business Volatility and uncertainty in general economic conditions may adversely affect our operating results and financial condition. Our business is sensitive to negative changes in general economic conditions, both inside and outside the U.S. Global and regional economic volatility and uncertainty, inflation and potential recession has and may continue to impact our business, resulting in: • increased cost to manufacture products or deliver solutions; • reduced customer purchasing power; • reduced demand for our solutions and services and reduced, delayed or canceled orders; • increased risk of excess and obsolete inventory; • increased risk of supply chain shortages; • increased price pressure on our solutions and services; and • greater risk of impairment to the value, and a detriment to the liquidity, of our future investment portfolio. In addition, global and regional macroeconomic developments, such as uncertainty related to future economic activity, increased tariff rates and reciprocal tariffs, volatility in financial and capital markets, reduced access to credit, changing interest rates, decreased liquidity, uncertain or destabilizing national elections and reactions to national election results, political violence and unrest in the U.S., the U.K., Europe, and Asia, and negative changes or volatility in general economic conditions in those regions could negatively affect our ability to conduct business in those territories. Financial difficulties experienced by our suppliers and customers due to economic volatility could result in product delays, reduced purchasing power, delays in payment or inability to pay us, and inventory issues. Economic risks related to accounts receivable could result in delays in collection and greater bad debt expense. Economic, political, and other risks associated with international sales and operations could adversely affect our results of operations. Because we operate our businesses and sell our solutions worldwide, our businesses are subject to risks associated with doing business internationally. We anticipate that revenue from international operations will continue to represent a majority of our total revenue. However, there can be no assurances that our international sales will continue at existing levels or grow in accordance with our effort to increase foreign market penetration. In addition, many of our employees, contract manufacturers, suppliers and manufacturing facilities are located outside the U.S. Accordingly, our future results could be negatively impacted by a variety of factors, including, but not limited to: • inability to conduct business in certain countries or regions or with certain customers due to U.S. sanctions or trade restrictions; • inability to sell certain products, technologies, or services to countries, regions, facilities, or customers due to sanctions or trade restrictions; • uncertainty regarding the U.S. government’s announced tariffs, potential changes to existing tariffs and whether additional tariffs may be imposed, modified or suspended; • changes in a specific country's

credit_strengths.text: Keysight's operating cash flow comfortably funds capital expenditure and the disclosed buyback, leaving substantial internal cash generation after reinvestment; free cash flow exceeds the repurchase programme, so discretionary returns are not reliant on incremental borrowing.

Liquidity is a clear strength: the current ratio sits well above the sector median and comfortably above unity, with cash balances covering a large share of reported debt, supporting a minimal indicative financial risk profile on both leverage and cash-flow tiers.

key_risks.text: Gross leverage rose year on year and now sits above the sector median, reflecting the step-up in reported debt alongside softer operating income; the acquisition outlay absorbed cash and pushed the balance sheet away from its prior conservative position.

The risk factors flag sensitivity to tariffs, export controls and reduced customer purchasing power across a business that earns most revenue internationally; such trade and demand shocks could compress margins and delay receivables collection, weakening the cash conversion that underpins current debt service.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage remains strong in absolute terms but declined year on year and trails the sector median, as operating income softened while gross interest expense held; EBITDA coverage shows the same direction, though both stay far above unity.

Free cash flow to debt improved slightly and edges above the sector median, while cash flow to debt slipped below both prior year and peer median; net leverage remains modest and well inside the next risk-band boundary, giving meaningful headroom against an EBITDA decline.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative profile is minimal risk, anchored by net leverage near the sector median and cash-flow coverage far above the downgrade threshold; the trajectory is mildly negative as gross leverage climbed and coverage ratios eased, so we would monitor deleveraging rather than expect deterioration.

Operating margin is below the sector median and narrowed year on year, so earnings quality rather than liquidity is the binding constraint; continued free cash flow generation and the absence of near-term maturities disclosed support a stable view, with acquisition integration the key swing factor.

credit_strengths.text: Keysight 的營運現金流足以輕鬆支付資本支出及已披露的回購，於再投資後仍留下大量內部現金生成；自由現金流超過回購計劃，因此酌情回報並不依賴增量借貸。
流動性為明顯優勢：流動比率遠高於行業中位數，並穩健地高於一，現金結餘覆蓋已報告債務的一大部分，於槓桿及現金流兩個層級均支持極低的指示性財務風險狀況。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿按年上升，現時高於行業中位數，反映已報告債務增加及營運收入轉弱；收購支出吸收了現金，並使資產負債表偏離其先前保守的狀況。
風險因素標示業務對關稅、出口管制及客戶購買力下降的敏感性，而該業務大部分收入來自國際市場；此類貿易及需求衝擊可能壓縮利潤率並延遲應收賬款回收，削弱支撐當前償債能力的現金轉換。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率絕對值仍然強勁，但按年下降並落後於行業中位數，因營運收入轉弱而總利息支出持平；EBITDA 覆蓋率顯示相同方向，惟兩者均遠高於一。
自由現金流對債務比率略有改善並略高於行業中位數，而現金流對債務比率則跌至低於去年及同業中位數；淨槓桿仍然溫和並穩處於下一風險區間邊界之內，對 EBITDA 下降提供有意義的緩衝。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性狀況為極低風險，錨定於淨槓桿接近行業中位數及現金流覆蓋率遠高於降級門檻；軌跡略為負面，因總槓桿攀升及覆蓋比率放緩，故我們將監察去槓桿而非預期惡化。
營運利潤率低於行業中位數並按年收窄，因此盈利質量而非流動性為約束因素；持續的自由現金流生成及未披露短期到期債務支持穩定觀點，而收購整合為關鍵變數。
